research_input_notes: FREQUENCY.md section 3 pairs for this chapter: RDS/Aurora vs DynamoDB; on-demand vs provisioned; DAX vs ElastiCache (chapter 29); GSI vs LSI; Aurora Global Database vs global tables; NAT gateway vs gateway endpoint (chapter 10). Stem signals: unpredictable or spiky (on-demand), microsecond read latency (DAX), key-value at any scale, multi-Region active-active, expire old items (TTL), LEAST operational overhead (serverless).
FRESHNESS.md hypotheses for this chapter are demand items of kind 'change'. Anything GA after 2026-07-15 is 'not examinable yet' (RULINGS rule 7).
Callvale (STARTUP.md chapter 28): table jobs, GSI by-customer, on-demand, TTL; stage 4 global tables and provisioned with auto scaling; DAX weighed and not chosen. Question stems never name Callvale.

demand.question: What are tables, items and attributes in DynamoDB, and is a table schemaless apart from the primary key attributes?
Which two kinds of primary key exist (partition key only; partition key plus sort key), and how does the partition key value decide the partition an item is stored in?
What is the maximum item size in DynamoDB (including attribute names and values) and does it include the index projections?
Is there any limit on the size of a table or on the number of items it can hold?
What is the default number of tables per account per Region, and the maximum that can be requested?
What is a hot partition (hot key), and why does an uneven partition key distribution cause throttling even when the table has spare capacity?
What is the maximum throughput one partition can serve (read capacity units and write capacity units per second)?
What is write sharding (adding a random or calculated suffix to the partition key) and when does the guide recommend it?
How should large objects (images, documents) be handled: store them in Amazon S3 and keep the key or pointer in the DynamoDB item?
Query versus Scan: which one uses the primary key or index key, which reads every item in the table, and why is Scan expensive on a large table?
Does a filter expression on a Query or Scan reduce the read capacity consumed, or is capacity charged for the items read before the filter?
What is the maximum size of one Query or Scan result page (1 MB) and how is a larger result set paginated (LastEvaluatedKey)?
What is a parallel scan, and how does the guide suggest limiting the impact of a scan on a production table (Limit, rate limiting, isolate with a GSI or a copy)?
Which data types does DynamoDB support (scalar: string, number, binary, Boolean, null; document: list, map; set types) and how deep can nesting go?
Which sort key conditions can a Query use (equals, less than, between, begins_with) and can a Query filter on the partition key with anything but equality?
What is PartiQL for DynamoDB and does it add joins across tables?
Eventually consistent versus strongly consistent reads: which is the default, how is a strongly consistent read requested (ConsistentRead), and what does eventual consistency mean in time terms?

How much more does a strongly consistent read cost than an eventually consistent one in capacity units (one RCU = one strongly consistent read or two eventually consistent reads of up to 4 KB per second)?
Which reads cannot be strongly consistent: reads from a global secondary index, reads through DAX, and cross-Region reads from a global table in eventual-consistency mode?

What do DynamoDB transactions provide (TransactWriteItems, TransactGetItems; all-or-nothing ACID across several items and tables in one Region) and what do they cost compared with standard reads and writes?
What is the maximum number of actions and the maximum aggregate size of one transaction (100 actions, 4 MB)?
What is a conditional write (ConditionExpression) and how does optimistic locking with a version attribute prevent lost updates?
What are the limits of BatchGetItem (100 items, 16 MB) and BatchWriteItem (25 put or delete requests, 16 MB)?
Does DynamoDB support atomic counters (ADD in an UpdateExpression) and are they idempotent?
What are the two throughput capacity modes (on-demand and provisioned), and what does each one ask the architect to decide?

Hypothesis (FRESHNESS): since the 2024-11-01 price cut AWS calls on-demand 'the default and recommended throughput option for most DynamoDB workloads'. What exactly does the capacity-mode page say, and what did older material assume (provisioned is cheaper, on-demand only for spiky traffic)?
On-demand mode: how is it billed (per read request unit and write request unit) and how does it react to a sudden rise in traffic (scales instantly up to what rule: double the previous peak)?
On-demand mode: what throughput does a new table get by default, how much can traffic grow before throttling (up to double the previous peak within 30 minutes), and what happens beyond that?

On-demand billing units: one write request unit = one write of up to 1 KB; one read request unit = one strongly consistent read of up to 4 KB (two eventually consistent reads); transactional requests cost two units?

Provisioned mode: one read capacity unit = one strongly consistent read per second of an item up to 4 KB (or two eventually consistent reads); one write capacity unit = one write per second of an item up to 1 KB?

How are item sizes rounded for capacity (reads to the next 4 KB, writes to the next 1 KB), and what is a worked example (for instance a 10 KB item: strongly consistent read 3 RCU, eventually consistent 1.5 RCU, write 10 WCU)?
What happens when a provisioned table receives more requests than its capacity (throttling, ProvisionedThroughputExceededException, SDK retries with exponential backoff)?
What is burst capacity: how many seconds of unused read and write capacity does DynamoDB retain (up to 300 seconds) and is it guaranteed?
What is adaptive capacity, does it act instantly, and does it isolate frequently accessed items on their own partitions?
How does DynamoDB auto scaling work for provisioned mode (Application Auto Scaling, target utilization, minimum and maximum capacity, CloudWatch alarms), and is it enabled by default in the console?
Auto scaling: what is the default target utilization (70 percent), and how fast can capacity be increased versus decreased?
How many times per day can provisioned capacity be decreased (4 at the start of the day plus 1 per hour, up to 27 per day) and is there a limit on increases?
Hypothesis (FRESHNESS 2025-08-12): how many times per 24 hours can a table switch between on-demand and provisioned mode (now 4; was once per 24 hours)?
Hypothesis (FRESHNESS 2024-05-01): on-demand tables can set a maximum throughput (maximum read and write request units) as a cost guardrail; what does it do when the limit is reached?

Default throughput quotas: per table 40,000 RCU and 40,000 WCU (or request units on demand); per account 80,000 provisioned; no account-level quota for on-demand tables?
Reserved capacity: for provisioned mode only, one-year or three-year terms, paid upfront, and does it apply to on-demand tables?

Kinesis Data Streams for DynamoDB: can records arrive out of order or more than once, and what retention can the Kinesis stream have?
